proposals: DGCI&S should publish Chapter 27 trade sub-totals for petroleum, coal, LNG and electricity in its standard commodity-wise release, so the US$203.4 billion import figure can be split by fuel without falling back on PPAC's product data, as this dashboard had to.

PPAC should publish the fortnightly benchmark averages and resulting import-parity, export-parity and trade-parity prices used to build refinery-gate prices for petrol and diesel, so the 80:20 formula can be checked without paid access to Platts Arab Gulf assessments.

PPAC should publish a monthly machine-readable series of realised import and export unit values for crude and each major petroleum product, so comparisons like crude's unit value against the Indian basket, and product-level grade divergence, can be tracked over time rather than in half-year snapshots.

CBIC should publish a consolidated effective-duty table for Chapter 27 tariff lines, showing BCD, AIDC, SWS, IGST and preferential FTA rates together, so an importer can cost a cargo like the base-oil example, at 30.98% effective, from one official source.
